<a id="vision"></a>

## Visual reasoning & graphics

<a id="visprog"></a>

### VisProg

**[Visual Programming: Compositional visual reasoning without training](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.11559)** · 2022-11

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Image + instruction → module program → answer or edited image |
| Mechanism | Turns a visual request into a sequence of predefined modules for tasks such as reasoning, recognition and image editing. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Intermediate module outputs expose where the reasoning goes wrong. |
| Design distinction | Its program language is organized around predefined visual modules with inspectable intermediate results; module interfaces constrain expressivity. |

**Related work:** [ViperGPT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.08128) · [PyVision](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.07998)

<a id="vipergpt"></a>

### ViperGPT

**[ViperGPT: Visual Inference via Python Execution for Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.08128)** · 2023-03

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Image/video + question → Python + visual APIs → answer |
| Mechanism | The code model sees API signatures and documentation, not implementations. GLIP localizes objects and X-VLM supplies attribute or image–text checks; regions and attributes become variables composed through ordinary Python control flow. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Visual modules return perceptual results; execution produces answers or localized regions with inspectable intermediate variables. |
| Experimental findings | In v1, zero-shot GQA test-dev accuracy is 48.1%, versus 44.7% for BLIP-2. This compares complete vision systems rather than isolating program representation. |
| Design distinction | Perception exposes properties and regions to the program; the interpreter performs sorting and filtering, with perception errors propagating into reasoning. |

**Related work:** [VisProg](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.11559) · [PyVision](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.07998)

**Source:** [v1, §§3–4.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2303.08128v1)

<a id="pyvision"></a>

### PyVision

**[PyVision: Agentic Vision with Dynamic Tooling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.07998)** · 2025-07

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Image + question → dynamically written tools → answer |
| Mechanism | Images are preloaded as variables. Generated code returns printed results and images for subsequent decisions. General Python libraries supply primitives; problem-specific pipelines and intermediate state persist across turns. |
| Feedback and evaluation | The executor returns text and images, which the vision model uses to inspect regions and calculations. |
| Experimental findings | Examples demonstrate thresholding, counting marks, auxiliary lines and histograms. These illustrate tool behavior rather than isolate component gains. |
| Design distinction | Tool implementations are generated per problem; flexibility comes from task-specific composition of general image libraries rather than a fixed perception API. |

**Related work:** [ViperGPT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.08128) · [VisProg](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.11559)

**Source:** [v1, §2 and tool-use examples](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.07998v1)

<a id="matplotagent"></a>

### MatPlotAgent

**[MatPlotAgent: Method and Evaluation for LLM-Based Agentic Scientific Data Visualization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.11453)** · 2024-02

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Plot request + data → plotting code → chart |
| Mechanism | Query expansion specifies data processing, functions and parameters. The code module permits three debugging rounds; GPT-4V critiques the request and draft, without seeing the reference used in evaluation. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Final evaluation uses GPT-4V reference-based scores from 0 to 100; the generation critic has different inputs. |
| Experimental findings | GPT-4 scores 48.86 directly, 61.16 with the framework and 53.44 without visual feedback. CodeLlama-34B instead declines under the full framework. |
| Design distinction | Runtime errors and visual defects use separate feedback; the generation critic sees the draft, while evaluation uses a reference figure. |

**Related work:** [ChartMimic](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.09961) · [JanusCoder](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.23538)

**Source:** [v1, §§3–5, Tables 1–2](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.11453v1)

<a id="januscoder"></a>

### JanusCoder

**[JanusCoder: Towards a Foundational Visual-Programmatic Interface for Code Intelligence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.23538)** · 2025-10

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Text/visual specification → multi-language code → rendered or computed result |
| Mechanism | Trains one code model on textual and visual program tasks; data-removal experiments expose both cross-task gains and interference. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Task evaluations and data-composition ablations test joint training. |
| Design distinction | Joint visual-program training exhibits both gains and interference; removing algorithmic data improves some ablation metrics. |

**Related work:** [MatPlotAgent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.11453) · [VisCodex](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.09945)

<a id="media"></a>

## Audio, video & documents

<a id="wavjourney"></a>

### WavJourney

**[WavJourney: Compositional Audio Creation with Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.14335)** · 2023-07

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Story description → audio script → compiled calls → mixed audio |
| Mechanism | Foreground events play sequentially; background events span foreground segments and characters map to voice presets. A fixed compiler expands the event list into generation, duration handling and mixing code. |
| Feedback and evaluation | GPT-4 organizes scripts; MusicGen, AudioGen and Bark generate music, effects and speech respectively. |
| Experimental findings | Story evaluation covers 50 titles across five genres, with human ratings of narrative relevance, pacing and other qualities of the complete pipeline. |
| Design distinction | The model outputs audio events and temporal relations; the compiler expands mixing operations, constraining editing to the script language. |

**Related work:** [WavCraft](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.09527) · [AudioAgent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.03335)

**Source:** [v2, §§3–5](https://arxiv.org/html/2307.14335v2)

<a id="wavcraft"></a>

### WavCraft

**[WavCraft: Audio Editing and Generation with Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.09527)** · 2024-03

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Recording + request → tool-using program → edited audio |
| Mechanism | Describes input recordings, then writes programs that combine expert tools for local audio edits and new compositions. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Audio descriptions guide decomposition; dialogue supports further edits. |
| Design distinction | Direct tool orchestration brings existing audio into analysis, editing and synthesis workflows; specialist models determine acoustic quality. |

**Related work:** [WavJourney](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.14335) · [AudioAgent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.03335)

<a id="slidecoder"></a>

### SlideCoder

**[SlideCoder: Layout-aware RAG-enhanced Hierarchical Slide Generation from Design](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.07964)** · 2025-06

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Design image + assets → python-pptx → editable single slide |
| Mechanism | CGSeg uses gradients and connected regions to form hierarchical blocks. Global and local descriptions guide generation; H-RAG retrieves shape types and operation functions before layout-constrained assembly. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Execution errors trigger repair; evaluation measures executability, local structure and global visual similarity separately. |
| Experimental findings | Slide2Code contains 300 slides in three complexity groups. On SLIDESBENCH, GPT-4o SlideCoder scores 78.8 overall versus 66.9 for the best baseline; this is a composite layout score. |
| Design distinction | Supplied designs and image assets constrain reconstruction; decomposition reduces per-call generation complexity, while Paper2Poster must also select content. |

**Related work:** [Paper2Poster](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.21497) · [Table2LaTeXRL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.17589)

**Source:** [v1, §§3–5, Table 1](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.07964v1)

<a id="paper2poster"></a>

### Paper2Poster

**[Paper2Poster: Towards Multimodal Poster Automation from Scientific Papers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.21497)** · 2025-05

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Paper → content/layout tree → generated presentation code → poster |
| Mechanism | A parser builds section synopses and figure assets. The planner uses content length, reading order and aspect ratios for panel allocation; Painter compresses text and invokes fixed code generation, while Commenter critiques individual panels. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Panel renders guide layout revision; final evaluation combines visual metrics, model judging and PaperQuiz content questions. |
| Experimental findings | PaperQuiz asks vision models 100 factual and interpretive questions derived from the paper. The image-generation baseline has high visual similarity but poor textual coherence. |
| Design distinction | Models select content and plan layout; a fixed generator constructs drawing code, bounded by templates and helper functions. |

**Related work:** [SlideCoder](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.07964) · [Paper2Video](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05096)

**Source:** [v1, §§3.3–5.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2505.21497v1)

<a id="code2video"></a>

### Code2Video

**[Code2Video: A Code-centric Paradigm for Educational Video Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.01174)** · 2025-10

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Teaching topic → storyboard + Manim → animation |
| Mechanism | Plans an educational video as a storyboard, generates Manim scenes, and revises the animation through visual critique. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Rendered scenes provide visual feedback for revision. |
| Design distinction | Animation programs control objects, motion and timing; Paper2Video focuses on combining slides, narration and audio. |

**Related work:** [Paper2Video](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05096) · [SlideCoder](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.07964)

<a id="table2latexrl"></a>

### Table2LaTeXRL

**[Table2LaTeX-RL: High-Fidelity LaTeX Code Generation from Table Images via Reinforced Multimodal Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.17589)** · 2025-09

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Table image → LaTeX → compiled table |
| Mechanism | Trains image-to-LaTeX table generation with rewards from compilation, rendered similarity and table structure. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Compilation failures receive zero reward; visual and structural scores evaluate successful renders. |
| Design distinction | Training rewards combine rendered and structural feedback; cell content, merge structure and appearance are distinct reconstruction dimensions. |

**Related work:** [SlideCoder](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.07964) · [MatPlotAgent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.11453)

<a id="spatial"></a>

## 3D, CAD & scene reconstruction

<a id="cadrecode"></a>

### CADRecode

**[CAD-Recode: Reverse Engineering CAD Code from Point Clouds](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.14042)** · 2024-12

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Point cloud → CadQuery Python → parametric solid |
| Mechanism | CadQuery supplies coordinate systems, sketches and solid operations. A lightweight point projector is trained jointly with the language model; different point samples produce candidates selected by executed geometry. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Evaluation reports surface Chamfer distance, volumetric IoU and invalid-program rate; candidate selection uses the input cloud. |
| Experimental findings | Switching from 160k DeepCAD examples to one million synthetic examples raises DeepCAD/Fusion360 IoU from 80.7/67.6 to 92.0/87.8, identifying training data as a major variable. |
| Design distinction | The output retains sketch and extrusion parameters; a matching surface can admit multiple construction histories. |

**Related work:** [DeepCAD](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.09492) · [Real2Code](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.08474)

**Source:** [v2, §§3–5, Table 1](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.14042v2)

<a id="real2code"></a>

### Real2Code

**[Real2Code: Reconstruct Articulated Objects via Code Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.08474)** · 2024-06

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Visual observations → parts + joint code → articulated object |
| Mechanism | Fine-tuned SAM segments articulated parts and a completion network recovers meshes. Box centers, orientations and half-lengths feed 7B CodeLlama; helper functions convert predicted joint types and axis/edge indices into absolute parameters. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Surface, joint-type, axis and position errors are assessed separately; moving parts have one-degree-of-freedom joints observed in nonzero configurations. |
| Experimental findings | Part reconstruction uses 467 training and 35 test objects. Omitting shape completion degrades complex-furniture meshes; real RGB-object experiments are primarily qualitative. |
| Design distinction | Bounding-box priors discretize continuous joint-axis and position prediction; part geometry and axis-alignment assumptions affect joint accuracy. |

**Related work:** [CADRecode](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.14042) · [BlenderAlchemy](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.17672)

**Source:** [v2, §§3–4.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.08474v2)

<a id="blenderalchemy"></a>

### BlenderAlchemy

**[BlenderAlchemy: Editing 3D Graphics with Vision-Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.17672)** · 2024-04-26

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Existing scene + text/reference → edit sequence → revised render |
| Mechanism | Each round generates several scripts, executes and renders them, then selects through pairwise comparisons. Tweak explores numerical neighborhoods; Leap permits structural edits. Text tasks can use generated reference images. |
| Feedback and evaluation | GPT-4V generates edits and judges renders; DALL·E 3 supplies visual references for textual intentions. |
| Experimental findings | Text-based material editing uses four rounds of eight candidates from the same initial wood material, combining candidate search, visual judging and reference generation. |
| Design distinction | Search spans numerical parameters and program structure, with preferences judged from renders of an existing scene and its editable scripts. |

**Related work:** [Real2Code](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.08474) · [LL3M](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.08228)

**Source:** [v3, §3 and §4.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.17672v3)

<a id="digital"></a>

## Computer use & digital workflows

<a id="codeact"></a>

### CodeAct

**[Executable Code Actions Elicit Better LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.01030)** · 2024-02

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Task + tool interfaces → Python actions → environment changes |
| Mechanism | The LLM alternates reasoning and code actions, receiving interpreter output, results or errors. One action combines control flow and tool data flow without restating every intermediate value in separate calls. |
| Feedback and evaluation | API-Bank tests atomic calls; M3ToolEval contains 82 manually constructed tasks requiring composed calls and tools. |
| Experimental findings | On M3ToolEval, GPT-4-1106-preview achieves 74.4% with code, 52.4% with JSON and 53.7% with text; average turns are 5.5, 7.6 and 7.7 respectively. |
| Design distinction | Control and data flow remain inside the program, allowing direct reuse of intermediate tool outputs in compositional tasks. |

**Related work:** [TaskWeaver](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.17541) · [OpenHandsVersa](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.03011)

**Source:** [v4, §2, Tables 2–3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.01030v4)

<a id="openhandsversa"></a>

### OpenHandsVersa

**[Coding Agents with Multimodal Browsing are Generalist Problem Solvers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.03011)** · 2025-06

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Digital task → browsing + code execution → task result |
| Mechanism | Adds multimodal browsing to a coding-agent framework and evaluates the same framework on software, assistant and enterprise tasks. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Task success is evaluated separately on software, assistant and enterprise benchmarks. |
| Design distinction | Experiments assess task coverage under a shared framework; cross-task training gains require separate training comparisons. |

**Related work:** [CodeAct](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.01030) · [OSWorld](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.07972) · [GAIA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12983)

<a id="robotics"></a>

## Embodied agents & robotics

<a id="codeaspolicies"></a>

### CodeAsPolicies

**[Code as Policies: Language Model Programs for Embodied Control](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.07753)** · 2022-09

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Instruction + APIs → policy program → robot behavior |
| Mechanism | Translates language instructions into hierarchical Python policies, generating helper functions over supplied perception and control APIs. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Perception calls supply observations; low-level controllers execute the requested motion. |
| Design distinction | Generated programs directly compose robot APIs; VoxPoser constructs spatial objectives whose actions are computed by a motion planner. |

**Related work:** [VoxPoser](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.05973) · [RoboticProgrammer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.04268)

<a id="voxposer"></a>

### VoxPoser

**[VoxPoser: Composable 3D Value Maps for Robotic Manipulation with Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.05973)** · 2023-07

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Instruction + scene → value-map code → planned motion |
| Mechanism | Writes programs that turn language and visual observations into 3D value maps, which guide motion planning. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Perception updates spatial maps; the planner handles continuous motion. |
| Design distinction | Programs construct composable 3D value maps for trajectory optimization; perception, value maps and control introduce separate error sources. |

**Related work:** [CodeAsPolicies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.07753) · [Eureka](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.12931)

<a id="eureka"></a>

### Eureka

**[Eureka: Human-Level Reward Design via Coding Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.12931)** · 2023-10

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Task + environment code → reward function → trained policy |
| Mechanism | Environment implementation and task descriptions condition generation. Candidates expose individual reward components; training statistics become textual feedback for a new batch derived from the best reward. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Candidate fitness depends on the trained policy’s task performance; reward values supply diagnostic signals. |
| Experimental findings | v1 evaluates 10 robots and 29 Isaac Gym tasks, with five runs per environment, five rounds per run and 16 reward candidates per round, each requiring policy evaluation. |
| Design distinction | An outer loop searches reward programs while an inner loop trains control policies; candidate evaluation includes policy-training cost. |

**Related work:** [CodeAsPolicies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.07753) · [GenSim2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.03645)

**Source:** [v1, §§2–4](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.12931v1)

<a id="gensim2"></a>

### GenSim2

**[GenSim2: Scaling Robot Data Generation with Multi-modal and Reasoning LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.03645)** · 2024-10

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Task/asset specification → simulation code → demonstrations → policy |
| Mechanism | Generates simulation tasks and solvers, collects demonstrations, and trains point-cloud policies with synthetic and real data. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Real-robot evaluation compares real-only, simulated-only and combined training data. |
| Design distinction | Programs synthesize training demonstrations; real, simulated and mixed-data experiments differ in both source and demonstration count. |

**Related work:** [GenSim](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.01361) · [Eureka](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.12931)

<a id="voyager"></a>

### Voyager

**[Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16291)** · 2023-05

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Environment + task → JavaScript skill → growing skill library |
| Mechanism | Inventory, nearby entities and completed tasks condition the curriculum. The library stores code under description embeddings and retrieves five skills for a task; generation composes them with up to four iterations. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Environment progress, interpreter errors and GPT-4 task verification provide feedback; only verified programs enter the library. |
| Experimental findings | The mechanism operates under shared Minecraft rules and Mineflayer interfaces; experience accumulates in programs and retrieval context while model parameters remain fixed. |
| Design distinction | Skills are retrieved by language descriptions but reused as executable programs; shared Mineflayer APIs support cross-task composition. |

**Related work:** [DreamCoder](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.08381) · [AgentWorkflowMemory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.07429)

**Source:** [v2, §§2.1–2.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2305.16291v2)

<a id="roboticprogrammer"></a>

### RoboticProgrammer

**[Robotic Programmer: Video Instructed Policy Code Generation for Robotic Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.04268)** · 2025-01

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Observation + task + APIs → policy code → robot execution |
| Mechanism | RoboPro trains on video-derived code, then generates robot policies from observations and instructions; it also tests changed APIs. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Task-success tests include original, renamed and refactored interfaces. |
| Design distinction | Experiments perturb API names and structures separately; the program generator is specially trained and real-world tests use one robot platform. |

**Related work:** [CodeAsPolicies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.07753) · [ClosedLoopRobotSoftware](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19906)

<a id="worlds"></a>

## World models & environment construction

<a id="worldcoder"></a>

### WorldCoder

**[WorldCoder, a Model-Based LLM Agent: Building World Models by Writing Code and Interacting with the Environment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.12275)** · 2024-02

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Interaction history → transition/reward code → planner |
| Mechanism | φ₁ enforces observed-transition consistency; φ₂ requires a planner to find a positive-reward trajectory. REx allocates refinement among candidates; changed goals can reuse dynamics and refine rewards through planning constraints. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Interaction supplies counterexamples and planning checks reachability. Complex tasks use MCTS; AlfWorld also uses BM25-based partial reward shaping. |
| Experimental findings | Optimism has little effect in dense-reward Sokoban but is necessary for the harder no-transfer Minigrid and tested AlfWorld settings; merely prompting a new reward underperforms planning constraints. |
| Design distinction | Planning reachability supplements experience consistency, particularly for sparse rewards and new goals; learned dynamics can be reused across goals. |

**Related work:** [GIFMCTS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15383) · [CodeAct](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.01030) · [Code2World](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09856)

**Source:** [v3, §§2–3, Figures 3–5](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.12275v3)

<a id="gifmcts"></a>

### GIFMCTS

**[Generating Code World Models with Large Language Models Guided by Monte Carlo Tree Search](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15383)** · 2024-05

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Transition examples → searched simulator code → model-based planning |
| Mechanism | Nodes store partial or complete model code, completed and executed on expansion. Prediction mismatches trigger Improve; syntax or runtime errors trigger successive Fix actions rather than immediate rejection. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Offline transitions score next state, reward and termination; planners measure return separately. CWMB uses deterministic, fully observable environments. RTFM fixes the manual and monster positions. |
| Experimental findings | With Llama-3-70B and 50 calls, discrete accuracy/normalized return are 0.84/0.76 versus 0.79/0.60 for a WorldCoder-v1-based baseline. Simplified RTFM accuracy with the same model and budget improves but return remains −0.11. |
| Design distinction | Code repair is a distinct tree-search action; model prediction scores and downstream planning returns are evaluated separately. |

**Related work:** [WorldCoder](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.12275) · [Code2World](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09856)

**Source:** [v2, §§3–5, Tables 2–4](https://arxiv.org/html/2405.15383v2)

<a id="code2world"></a>

### Code2World

**[Code2World: A GUI World Model via Renderable Code Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09856)** · 2026-02

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | GUI screenshot + action → HTML → predicted next screen |
| Mechanism | Predicts the next GUI observation by generating renderable HTML from a screenshot and an action, then uses the prediction for decisions. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Rendered observations are evaluated with downstream GUI-task performance. |
| Design distinction | Predicts the interface observation after an action; WorldCoder predicts state transitions and rewards queried by a planner. |

**Related work:** [WorldCoder](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.12275) · [ProgrammableWorldModel](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10540)

<a id="programmableworldmodel"></a>

### ProgrammableWorldModel

**[Programmable World Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10540)** · 2026-09

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | World state + action → state update → neural video |
| Mechanism | Maintains persistent entity state and rules in programs while a pretrained video model renders the resulting observations. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Reported checks include visible entity counts and entity state. |
| Design distinction | Explicit state and image generation are separate components; entity identity, persistent relations and visual quality form distinct evaluation dimensions. |

**Related work:** [CodeWorldBrain](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.25927) · [Code2World](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09856)

<a id="math"></a>

## Mathematics & formal proofs

<a id="pal"></a>

### PAL

**[PAL: Program-aided Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.10435)** · 2022-11

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Word problem → program → computed answer |
| Mechanism | Prompt examples pair questions with programmatic steps; answers come from execution. Comments express explanations while variables and operations encode quantities and relations, executed as a complete computation chain. |
| Feedback and evaluation | The basic procedure generates and executes a program once, without an iterative error-repair loop. |
| Experimental findings | Appendix B reports 72.0% with execution versus 23.2% when the model simulates the runtime. Appendix A separately shows effects from meaningful variable names and comments. |
| Design distinction | The model generates the problem representation and computation steps; the interpreter computes precisely, while semantic errors can remain in variable relations. |

**Related work:** [PoT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.12588) · [ChainOfCode](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.04474)

**Source:** [PDF, §3; Appendices A–B, Tables 4 and 6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2211.10435)

<a id="chainofcode"></a>

### ChainOfCode

**[Chain of Code: Reasoning with a Language Model-Augmented Code Emulator](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.04474)** · 2023-12

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Reasoning task → code + emulated steps → answer |
| Mechanism | Interleaves real program execution with a language-model emulator for semantic steps that ordinary code cannot directly execute. |
| Feedback and evaluation | An interpreter and a language-model emulator jointly advance the program. |
| Design distinction | An interpreter handles executable steps while a language model simulates undefined semantic operations, whose errors propagate downstream. |

**Related work:** [PAL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.10435) · [PoT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.12588)

<a id="leandojo"></a>

### LeanDojo

**[LeanDojo: Theorem Proving with Retrieval-Augmented Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.15626)** · 2023-06

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Formal statement + library → tactics → checked proof |
| Mechanism | Program analysis determines accessible premises. Dense retrieval matches proof states to premises; the generator conditions on both to propose tactics. Training includes hard negatives from the positive premise’s source file. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Tactic execution returns local contexts and goals, or errors such as timeouts and inapplicable tactics; best-first search organizes proof steps. |
| Experimental findings | Accessibility analysis reduces average candidate premises from about 128k to 33k. The novel_premises split requires premises unused in training proofs, testing a different generalization setting from random theorem splits. |
| Design distinction | A retriever selects available premises for a proof state; the generator proposes tactics and receives Lean states. Retrieval and proof search can be trained and evaluated separately. |

**Related work:** [DeepSeekProverV2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.21801) · [AlphaProof](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09833-y)

**Source:** [PDF, §§4–5; novel_premises split](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.15626)

<a id="deepseekproverv2"></a>

### DeepSeekProverV2

**[DeepSeek-Prover-V2: Advancing Formal Mathematical Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning for Subgoal Decomposition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.21801)** · 2025-04

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Formal theorem → subgoals + proof code → Lean verification |
| Mechanism | Dependency-ordered subgoals become lemmas, with earlier ones available as premises. Variants with and without these premises form a curriculum; composed proofs pair with V3 reasoning before GRPO training. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Lean 4.9.0 verifies proofs; binary correctness rewards and early consistency rewards connect final proofs to decomposed lemmas. |
| Experimental findings | The 671B CoT model reaches 82.4% pass@32 and 88.9% pass@8192 on MiniF2F-test, with a 256-fold difference in sampling budget. |
| Design distinction | Subgoals support both proof completion and curriculum construction; the final model combines informal reasoning with Lean proof generation. |

**Related work:** [LeanDojo](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.15626) · [AlphaProof](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09833-y)

**Source:** [v1, §§2–3.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.21801v1)

<a id="alphaproof"></a>

### AlphaProof

**[Olympiad-level formal mathematical reasoning with reinforcement learning](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09833-y)** · 2025-11-12

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Formalized problem → proof search/adaptation → Lean proof |
| Mechanism | Combines Lean proof search, reinforcement learning and test-time adaptation to tackle difficult formalized mathematics problems. |
| Feedback and evaluation | The proof assistant supplies verification during learning and search. |
| Design distinction | Formal verification supplies both training and search feedback; the IMO setting includes human formalization and extended test-time computation. |

**Related work:** [DeepSeekProverV2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.21801) · [LeanDojo](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.15626)

<a id="science"></a>

## Scientific & algorithmic discovery

<a id="funsearch"></a>

### FunSearch

**[Mathematical discoveries from program search with large language models](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06924-6)** · 2023-12-14

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Skeleton + evaluator → candidate function → scored construction |
| Mechanism | Programs from one island are ordered by score as function versions, prompting the next version. Invalid candidates are discarded; weaker islands are periodically restarted from stronger individuals to sustain exploration. |
| Feedback and evaluation | An evaluator executes the solver skeleton and checks output validity and score; experience resides in program populations, with model weights fixed. |
| Experimental findings | For eight-dimensional cap sets, search finds a program generating 512 vectors; manual simplification yields an explicit construction. This establishes a constructive lower bound, with human analysis in interpretation. |
| Design distinction | Search operates on functions that construct solutions; externally evaluated candidates enter a population while model weights remain fixed. |

**Related work:** [AlphaEvolve](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13131) · [LLMSR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.18400)

**Source:** [FunSearch method; Extremal combinatorics, Figure 4](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06924-6)

<a id="alphaevolve"></a>

### AlphaEvolve

**[AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13131)** · 2025-06

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Initial program + evaluator → program evolution → improved candidate |
| Mechanism | Combines language-model proposals, a population of programs and automatic evaluators to improve algorithms and mathematical constructions. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Task-specific checks establish validity and score each candidate. |
| Design distinction | Compared with FunSearch, edits extend to larger code components and algorithm implementations; evaluators define objectives and validity. |

**Related work:** [FunSearch](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06924-6) · [AlphaDev](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06004-9)

<a id="llmsr"></a>

### LLMSR

**[LLM-SR: Scientific Equation Discovery via Programming with Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.18400)** · 2024-04

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Observed data → equation program + fitted parameters → prediction |
| Mechanism | Programs take observations and a params vector; coefficients are fitted before error-based scoring. Island populations retain search diversity, cluster by score and favor shorter programs when sampling prompt examples. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Negative MSE drives search; ID/OOD NMSE separately measure fitting and prediction outside the observed region. |
| Experimental findings | On Oscillation 2, removing problem descriptions raises OOD NMSE from 3.81×10⁻⁵ to 7.10×10⁻³; removing coefficient optimization raises it to 0.378. |
| Design distinction | Discrete structure search is separated from continuous coefficient fitting; variable semantics in language supply a search prior. |

**Related work:** [FunSearch](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06924-6) · [LLMFeynman](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.06512)

**Source:** [v2, §§2, 4–5, Table 1](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.18400v2)

<a id="coscientist"></a>

### Coscientist

**[Autonomous chemical research with large language models](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06792-0)** · 2023-12-20

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Chemistry task → tool/code workflow → physical experiment |
| Mechanism | Connects documentation retrieval, code execution and laboratory automation to plan and carry out chemistry experiments. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Laboratory measurements provide feedback alongside computational tools. |
| Design distinction | Evaluation includes physical chemistry experiments; instrument APIs, documentation retrieval and laboratory configuration are parts of the system. |

**Related work:** [ChemCrow](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.05376) · [AIScientistV2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.08066)

<a id="scienceagentbench"></a>

### ScienceAgentBench

**[ScienceAgentBench: Toward Rigorous Assessment of Language Agents for Data-Driven Scientific Discovery](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.05080)** · 2024-10

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Scientific task + data → analysis code → evaluated result |
| Mechanism | Tasks provide data and output requirements; dedicated evaluators check predictions, test performance or figures. Successful execution and saving precede task success; human rubrics assess stages from processing through output saving. |
| Feedback and evaluation | GPT-4o judges figure tasks against references; code similarity, execution and task outcomes are reported separately. |
| Experimental findings | Claude-3.5-Sonnet self-debugging with knowledge and best-of-three reaches 86.3% execution and 34.3% success, versus 92.2%/32.4% without knowledge: task success improves while execution declines. |
| Design distinction | Measures execution, task outputs and cost; adding domain knowledge can improve task success while lowering valid execution. |

**Related work:** [SciCode](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.13168) · [DiscoveryBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.01725)

**Source:** [v1, §§2–4, Table 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.05080v1)

<a id="aiscientistv2"></a>

### AIScientistV2

**[The AI Scientist-v2: Workshop-Level Automated Scientific Discovery via Agentic Tree Search](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.08066)** · 2025-04

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Research direction → experiment code/search → results + manuscript |
| Mechanism | Uses experiment-tree search to organize machine-learning experiments, then turns the results into a paper. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Experiment results guide further exploration; selected manuscripts enter review. |
| Design distinction | The workflow spans experiment design, execution and writing; paper selection and external review remain separate stages. |

**Related work:** [AIScientist](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.06292) · [ScienceAgentBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.05080)

<a id="foundations"></a>

## Shared foundations, tools & skills

<a id="dreamcoder"></a>

### DreamCoder

**[DreamCoder: Growing generalizable, interpretable knowledge with wake-sleep Bayesian program learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.08381)** · 2020-06

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Task examples → synthesized programs → reusable library |
| Mechanism | Wake searches using task likelihood and program priors; abstraction refactors solutions into reusable subroutines; dreaming trains a recognition model on replayed tasks and tasks generated by sampling library programs. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Task behavior constrains candidate programs and description length constrains library growth; the recognition model and symbolic library improve together. |
| Experimental findings | The sorting example in Figure 1 uses five library calls after six iterations, versus 32 calls when expanded into initial primitives. Evaluations span eight domains. |
| Design distinction | Library learning compresses shared structure in solved programs and changes later synthesis search spaces; Voyager primarily retrieves complete skills. |

**Related work:** [Voyager](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16291) · [SketchAdapt](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.06349)

**Source:** [v1, Wake/Sleep Program Learning, pp. 4–6; Figure 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2006.08381v1)

<a id="react"></a>

### ReAct

**[ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629)** · 2022-10

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Task → reasoning/action/observation sequence → result |
| Mechanism | Alternates reasoning text and tool actions, using new observations to update subsequent decisions. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Environment observations enter the next reasoning step. |
| Design distinction | Observations enter between reasoning and action, grounding later decisions in environment feedback; task interfaces define the action space. |

**Related work:** [CodeAct](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.01030) · [Reflexion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366)

<a id="reflexion"></a>

### Reflexion

**[Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11366)** · 2023-03

| Aspect | Analysis |
|---|---|
| Input and output | Task feedback → textual reflection → next attempt |
| Mechanism | Stores language reflections on failed or completed attempts as context for later attempts. |
| Feedback and evaluation | Feedback is converted into a memory of what to change. |
| Design distinction | Failures are summarized in cross-attempt language memory; reuse requires model interpretation, unlike directly executable skill libraries. |

**Related work:** [Voyager](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16291) · [ReAct](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629)
